analysis.title: DB CoTD: One Week On, Several Plot Twists Later
key_insights: One week after the midterm elections the S&P 500 is down just -0.6% on the week, but the path was volatile: +1.58% the day after the vote (best day in three months), then -4.36% the next session (biggest daily slump since the week of the April 2025 Liberation Day tariff announcements), then +2.35% on Monday (best day since the April Iran ceasefire announcement).

Beneath the flat index there are clear winners and losers. Tech is -4.3% over the week, with the stocks most exposed to AI doing worst. The Philly semiconductor index is -5.7% since the midterms, partly on expectations of tougher AI regulation.

Relative winners since the vote: solar stocks (MAC Global Solar Energy Index +1.4% since the Democratic sweep), the STOXX 600 (+2.0%, helped by Europe's smaller AI exposure), and the Hang Seng Tech index (+5.6% in the week after the vote, possibly a rotation from US AI into China AI, though it slipped back today). MSCI EM is broadly steady.

Brent crude fell -11.7% in the week after the midterms to its lowest close since August. The expected post-midterm escalation in the Middle East has not happened and rhetoric has leaned towards de-escalation. Prices are edging higher today.
The 2yr Treasury yield rose +17.6bps on the post-CPI reaction yesterday, its biggest move higher since the Liberation Day tariffs were postponed by 90 days.
DB's summary of the market's one-week verdict: the election result is read as relatively bad for AI and good for lower energy prices.

DB's equity strategists give the devil's advocate case: US tech positioning is now very low relative to recent years, and a deal with Iran still looks a long way off, so the trade may have further twists.
